newsitem.title: GERMANY: German builders desert Transrapid project - paper.
newsitem.headline: German builders desert Transrapid project - paper.

text.p: Germany's largest construction groups are quitting the consortium set up to design and build the nine-billion-mark ($5.26 billion) Transrapid Hamburg-to-Berlin rail network, a newspaper said on Friday.
The Munich-based Sueddeutsche Zeitung said Phillip Holzmann AG, Hochtief AG and Bilfinger+Berger AG were leaving the Transrapid consortium.
The remaining partners, engineering group Thyssen AG and Siemens AG, would as a result have to inject some 500 million marks into the project, it said.
The Deutsche Bahn railways would meanwhile have to take on greater financial risk relating to the level of future receipts from the track, the paper added.

The Transrapid fast rail network, which uses magnetic levitation technology, has come under criticism both as to whether there is sufficient demand for it in Germany and whether it can justify the six billion marks of state funding Bonn plans to offer for it.
